pronunciation.approximation: Say "pachamama" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Pachamama".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "pachamama" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Pachamama" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Pachamama
domains.subtitle: Earth
domains.lead: Pachamama is earth, harvest, mother. The name means "Mother Earth" and belongs to the incan tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Pachamama returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in incan myth, cult, and cultural memory.

cards.name: Unicode Restoration
cards.desc: Preserved as a flagship temple despite the unregistrable plain-ASCII form.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.meaning: The restored form Pachamama, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Pachamama place earth, harvest, mother at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Pachamama appears in incan tradition as earth, harvest, mother. The name's meaning, "Mother Earth", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Pachamama in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Pachamama remains a touchstone for understanding incan religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Bauer, Brian S., The Sacred Landscape of the Inca (1998).
Moseley, Michael E., The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001).
